1.21 Recovery after a failure

First determine whether a process is still alive and whether its outputs show actual progress or a terminal error. A stale status file or a command timeout is not proof that the job died. Never start another archive owner because a progress line has been quiet.

Retain the failed report, logs, checkpoint and source version. Rerun the same qualified owner only after its prior process is gone and the source/reference scope still matches. Do not turn an exception into a fabricated equal result. For a decoder failure, use a supported codec/layout or retain the exact original. For a source identity change, determine whether software wrote metadata and start a new qualified comparison rather than weakening the guard.

Temporary .partial, .tmp or .recovery-partial files are incomplete unless their normal owner finished verification and commit. A payload in an archive folder is not sufficient evidence that the whole archive completed. Check the manifest, checkpoint, final summary and restore. For reference-backed storage, check both delta/original payload and the required reference version.

Before deleting any source tree through a separate process, account for all regular files and sidecars, renamed candidates, unique metadata/settings, filesystem attributes, catalog locations and the required independent copies. Perform a verified restore on representative changed and missing-reference cases. A true raw subsumption verdict is useful evidence, but is only one part of that decision.
